questions.enonce_markdown:
Comment on the discussion between Jesus and the woman at the well.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** The conversation in John 4:1-42 takes place at Jacob's well near the Samaritan town of Sychar. It is a long dialogue in which Jesus moves from an ordinary request for water to the revelation of who he is, and it ends with many Samaritans coming to faith.

**1. Breaking social barriers.** It was about the sixth hour, around midday, when Jesus, tired from the journey, asked a Samaritan woman for a drink (4:6-7). She is surprised, for "Jews do not share things in common with Samaritans" (4:9), and the disciples are amazed that he speaks with a woman (4:27). By speaking to a woman and a Samaritan, Jesus crosses boundaries of nation, religion and gender.

**2. Living water.** Jesus says that if she knew who was asking, she would ask him and he would give her "living water" (4:10). The water of the well satisfies only for a time, but the water he gives will become "a spring of water gushing up to eternal life" (4:13-14). Living water here stands for the life and Spirit given by Jesus. The woman at first misunderstands, taking it literally, and asks for the water so that she will not have to come to the well.

**3. Her personal life.** Jesus asks her to call her husband and tells her that she has had five husbands and now lives with a man who is not her husband (4:16-18). This shows that he knows her situation, and it leads her to say, "Sir, I see that you are a prophet" (4:19). Jesus' knowledge leads her to recognition, not to condemnation.

**4. The question of worship.** The woman raises the old dispute between Jews and Samaritans over the right place for worship, Mount Gerizim or Jerusalem (4:20). Jesus answers that the hour is coming when true worshippers will worship the Father "in spirit and truth" (4:21-24). Worship is therefore not tied to a place but depends on a right relationship with God, who is spirit.

**5. Revelation of the Messiah.** The woman says that she knows that the Messiah is coming. Jesus replies, "I am he, the one who is speaking to you" (4:25-26). This is one of the clearest self-declarations in the Gospel, and it is made to a Samaritan woman.

**6. Witness and faith.** She leaves her water jar and tells the townspeople, "Come and see" (4:28-29). Many Samaritans believe because of her word, and then more because they hear him themselves, saying that he is "the Saviour of the world" (4:39-42). Jesus tells the disciples that his food is to do the will of the one who sent him (4:34).

**Conclusion.** The discussion shows Jesus as the giver of living water and the Messiah, who offers salvation beyond the limits of Jew and Samaritan, man and woman, and who calls for worship in spirit and truth. It also presents the woman as an early witness whose testimony leads others to faith.
